title: Patan Patola Heritage Museum - Preserving Gujarat’s Timeless Weaving Art
content:
Patan Patola Heritage Museum

Located in the historic city of Patan, Gujarat, the Patan Patola Heritage Museum is a living tribute to one of India’s most intricate and ancient weaving arts - the Patola saree. Established by the Salvi family, who have been preserving this craft for over 700 years, the museum showcases the unmatched beauty, skill, and patience behind this double ikat weaving tradition.

About Patola Weaving

Patola sarees are handwoven using the double ikat technique, where both the warp and weft threads are dyed separately before weaving. The process demands months of precision, as even a tiny mistake can disturb the pattern. Traditionally, these sarees were worn by royal families and are considered symbols of luxury and auspiciousness.

Inside the Museum

The museum offers visitors a rare opportunity to witness the entire process of Patola weaving, from dyeing to thread alignment. It also displays ancient looms, traditional tools, old photographs, and rare Patola designs passed down through generations. Visitors can even interact with the Salvi weavers, who explain the secrets behind the art that takes four to six months to complete a single saree.

Location

The Patan Patola Heritage Museum is located near Rani ki Vav in Patan, making it easy to explore both sites in one visit.

Timings & Entry Fee

  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Around ₹20 - ₹50 per person
  • Closed: Usually open all days, but check before visiting on public holidays.

Best Time to Visit

Visit between October and February for pleasant weather and comfortable sightseeing around Patan.

  • Panchasara Jain Temple (2 km) - Beautiful Jain temple with marble carvings.
